answer: Anchor every agent identity to a refundable stake that grows in terraces: a new agent starts on a low terrace with limited spending, and only after a history of honest trades can it climb higher. Creating a fake identity costs a fresh stake, so flooding the network with islands of fake accounts becomes expensive. Peers also share a reef of reputation — when one identity is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and linked accounts lose trust. Honest agents pay once and trade freely; an attacker must pay for every fake, again and again.
